questions.question: How do Bundler and the Gemfile work together?
questions.title: Bundler and the Gemfile
questions.direct_answer: The Gemfile lists the gems you want; Bundler resolves compatible versions and installs them, recording the exact versions in Gemfile.lock. Workflow: add a gem line to the Gemfile (gem 'sidekiq'), run bundle install (which resolves, installs, and updates the lock), commit BOTH Gemfile and Gemfile.lock, and run your app with bundle exec. The Gemfile is your intent (what you want, with version constraints); the lock is the resolved reality (exact versions). If two gems need conflicting versions, Bundler reports a conflict and you resolve it by loosening a constraint.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know the Gemfile is intent (constraints) and the lock is the resolved reality (exact versions), and the workflow (add, bundle install, commit both).
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Committing the Gemfile without Gemfile.lock (others resolve differently), or editing the lock by hand (Bundler owns it).
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Gemfile = intent (gem + constraint); Gemfile.lock = resolved exact versions. Add to Gemfile, bundle install, commit BOTH, run with bundle exec.

sections.title: Intent vs Resolved Reality
sections.content: The Gemfile lists the gems you want; Bundler resolves compatible versions and installs them, recording the exact versions in Gemfile.lock. Workflow: add a gem line to the Gemfile (gem sidekiq), run bundle install (which resolves, installs, and updates the lock), commit BOTH Gemfile and Gemfile.lock, and run your app with bundle exec. The Gemfile is your intent — what you want, with version constraints; the lock is the resolved reality — the exact versions that work together. If two gems need conflicting versions of a shared dependency, Bundler reports a conflict and you resolve it by loosening a constraint.

sections.title: Gemfile -> Bundler -> lock
sections.content:
The Gemfile is intent; the lock is the resolved exact versions.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  G[Gemfile: intent] --> B[bundle install: resolve + install]
  B --> L[Gemfile.lock: exact versions]
  L --> C[commit both; bundle exec to run]
```

sections.title: The workflow
sections.content:
```ruby
# 1) Add the gem to the Gemfile
echo "gem 'sidekiq'" >> Gemfile

# 2) Resolve and install (updates the lock)
bundle install

# 3) Commit BOTH files together
git add Gemfile Gemfile.lock
git commit -m 'add sidekiq for background jobs'

# 4) Run with the locked versions
bundle exec sidekiq

# The Gemfile is intent (constraints):
#   gem 'rails', '~> 7.0'
# The lock is the resolved reality (exact):
#   rails (7.0.8)
#     actionpack (= 7.0.8)
#     ...

# A conflict: Bundler reports it; you loosen a constraint to resolve.
# DON'T edit Gemfile.lock by hand — Bundler owns it.
```

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Committing the Gemfile without Gemfile.lock — others resolve differently.
Editing Gemfile.lock by hand — Bundler owns it; regenerate with bundle install.
Forgetting bundle exec — loads system gems, not the locked versions.

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Gemfile lists the gems you want (intent, with version constraints).
Bundler resolves compatible versions and records exact ones in Gemfile.lock (reality).
Workflow: add to Gemfile, bundle install, commit BOTH, run with bundle exec.
Commit Gemfile AND Gemfile.lock together so everyone resolves identically.
Bundler owns the lock — don't edit it by hand; regenerate with bundle install.

If two gems need conflicting versions of a shared dependency, Bundler reports a conflict and you resolve it by loosening a constraint.
